findings.title: Use demand V_provider in every chip and gas card after separating fixed provider reference
findings.reason: The complete measurement rule, cp_feed and calculations reserve fixed A_provider for provider reference and V_provider for converted period demand, but chip quantity conditions/cards still say convert to A and use reference volume A per1kg; gas card similarly uses reference volume A. The old A notation and new explicit fixed reference are left inconsistent in the same quantity contract.
findings.consequence: A consumer can use a fixed1m3 provider reference as the demanded quantity even when actual period demand is10m3. The explicit calc rule is correct, so the defect is an incomplete symbol migration in card instructions, not the underlying state-conversion algebra.
findings.requested_correction: Reserve A_provider for fixed provider reference; update every chip/gas preamble, card amount and cp_fuel/reference phrase to converted period V_provider, exchangeV_provider/Q and separate n_provider=V_provider/A_provider. Regenerate projection and keep state/definition gaps.
findings.limits: A may have been intended as shorthand for demand in old cards. The new rule removes that meaning, so this is a confirmed cross-field ambiguity; no measured downstream wrong quantity is claimed.
